note: Vocabulary the publication-boundary check keeps out of this repository.
`prose` is stated plainly because stating it discloses nothing: it is true of any
library that its source and its documentation describe behaviour, and that money
modelling and issue-tracker identifiers belong in the systems that own them.
`paths` and `content` are digests rather than words, so that this file does not
become the list it exists to keep out. Each entry is the first 16 hex characters of
the SHA-256 of a normalised phrase: lower-cased, runs of digits replaced by '#',
every other non-letter collapsed to a single space. The checker normalises candidate
text the same way and compares. Digests are obscurity, not secrecy -- the point is
that the file carries no readable inventory, not that the entries are unguessable.
`paths` is prefix-matched against each normalised path segment, so a copy one
directory down does not escape it. `content` is matched against every 1-, 2- and
3-word window of every line of every tracked file. `prose` is matched against file
A failure prints the file, the line and the text that matched, so nobody needs to
reverse an entry to know what to change. The fix is always the same: rewrite the
sentence so it states the engineering fact.
